text:
maria.arch: Quick question — the RFC suggests moving most delivery safety checks into the control plane before we produce delta bundles. For on‑prem / airgapped installs that only talk to a local operator, does that mean the operator must implement the same policy engine? How do we keep operator UX simple when we want strict safety guarantees?

anna.dev: Short answer: we need a small local policy adapter, not the full control plane. Operator should validate a compact policy blob and signatures, not run all policy logic.

sam.platform: Agreed. Tradeoffs: putting checks only in control plane gives us centralized observability but breaks airgapped installs unless we ship a tiny verifier.

lee.sre: +1. Also watch resource limits — many customer nodes are low RAM. Any verifier must be <50MB resident and constant CPU spikes are bad.

anna.dev: Proposal: embed a compact manifest that contains: policy-hash, signer-key-id, allowed-ops list. Operator verifies manifest signature and hash locally. Full policy evaluation stays in control plane when available.

anna.dev: Example minimal manifest snippet we discussed:```yaml
manifest_version: 1
policy_hash: "sha256:..."
signer: "kms://projects/company/keys/updater"
allowed_ops:
  - activate
  - dry-run
  - rollback
```

maria.arch: That looks reasonable. How do we handle rollbacks if operator rejects a bundle because it lacks policy audit metadata? Do we want a grace-mode for older installs?

sam.platform: We should support a compatibility flag in the operator: "compat-mode: permissive|strict|audit-only". Default for new installs is strict; for upgrades we allow permissive with telemetry off by default. Then surface warnings in console.

lee.sre: If we add permissive mode, we must make it explicit in upgrade docs and require operator-initiated confirmation. Otherwise ops teams will inadvertently accept insecure bundles.

maria.arch: Sounds like next steps: 1) define the compact manifest schema (anna to draft), 2) implement a tiny verifier library (anna + sam), 3) operator adds compat-mode flag and a one‑time interactive upgrade flow, 4) create migration playbook for customers.

anna.dev: I'll open a PR with schema draft today and a PoC verifier in Go. Will keep memory envelope low and no background polling.

sam.platform: I'll add the compat-mode flag to the operator RFC and sketch the console warnings. Also tagging rollout team for release gating.

lee.sre: Add a stress test for low‑spec VMs and for long offline periods (months). We need to ensure verifier still works after clock skew and expired CRLs.

deploy-bot: RFC updated: link to repo: https://git.redwood.internal/rfcs/compact-manifest. New commit by anna.dev.

maria.arch: Nice. @anna.dev @sam.platform let's sync tomorrow 11am PT in #architecture to walk the PoC. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face
